title: Tin whistle
summary: A Clare D tin whistle built only from the published measurements of one real whistle (ISVR, Southampton): its bore, six finger-hole diameters and spacings, the tapered flue channel, the window, the wedge and the closed pocket behind the flue, blown at the air flow the same paper measured for each note of the scale. Speaks; not graded (no licensed reference). Listening only: there is no licensed reference recording of a tin whistle yet, so no spectrogram comparison is made and nothing here claims to match a real whistle.
physics_present: fs-couple flue_loop: a jet driven by a blowing pressure that is computed from the published air flow of each note through the measured flue (viscous windway law), with the measured window length as the jet length, acting on a connected duct network (one jet drives the whole graph)
the measured cylindrical bore with six finger holes as plane-wave chimney sections on ideal junctions, open or closed per the published fingering chart, and the closed pocket behind the flue

the window's acoustic mass from its 3-D geometry: the 8 mm by 5.3 mm cut through the 2.4 mm wall of the 6.1 mm bore, with the pocket behind it and free space outside, solved as potential flow (fs_bem::wall_window, two grids extrapolated at the edges' order 4/3) and installed in place of the 0.61 a_eq mouth inertance: 15.71 mm of bore instead of 12.80 mm. In native renders with one binary it lowers the notes by 14 to 30 cents, 76 to 94 percent of the passive shift; F#5 moves 11 cents, half its passive shift

the measurement's gas: dry air at 20 C, because the paper blew the whistle from a regulated, metered air supply in a 20 C anechoic room, not by mouth (specimen.tsv). Breath temperature and humidity do not apply to this reference
fractional-delay propagation and gas-derived viscothermal loss on the long bore sections

radiation reaction and observation from the apertures themselves, so the sound is radiated pressure at a physical receiver rather than internal pressure: a compact baffled-piston load on every open hole and the open end, plus the window
a self-sustained oscillation: each note settles to a steady tone and re-rendering with another jet seed gives the same pitch and level, so it is a limit cycle and not a filtered seed

the register ladder of the all-holes-closed fingering at the air flows the paper measured for the second, third and fourth registers: the native renders sound the second, third and fourth modes of the pipe, each within a few tens of cents of the tempered note, at two mechanics clocks and two jet seeds. No parameter was adjusted to reach them, and the flows are the paper's, so the register selection of this windway jet follows the measured flow
physics_missing: a measured jet that sustains this whistle: the opt-in published jet transfer (Price, Johnston and McKinnon 2015 Eqs. 4 to 10, with the jet gain they fitted with the pipe flow blocked and the long-channel phase velocity measured by de la Cuadra) does NOT self-sustain at any of the paper's four ladder flows: all four renders are silent after the attack (gate 2 of pexfp.320, build a3e8bc48f; the register ladder above belongs to the interim slot-jet card, not to a measured jet). The same hosted loop does sustain on two plain-tube fixtures of the real island (tests/flue_nolle_loop.rs), and the whistle loop is live, not open: with every loss removed it sounds at the very frequency the linear tool predicts, and its line shapes at all four flows follow the tool's open-loop shape. But its strength on the whistle is an order of magnitude or more below the linear tool's, so the tool's predicted instability at the two higher flows does not appear. The gap is unresolved; it does not depend on the network structure (riser, pocket, stubs), is not the passive loss (native pole widths agree with the analytic ones), not the one-sample lag, not the alpha_j term, not the viscous windway path, and the module alone behaves as the tool says. The playing-condition jet gain is UNKNOWN (u-jet-playing-gain), so this is not a claim about a real whistle
any reference: no licensed recording of a tin whistle exists in the library yet (bead pexfp.219), so these renders are listened to, not graded, and no claim of resemblance is made

the register transitions themselves: only the paper's measured operating points were rendered, each from rest with the same onset ramp. The flow at which each register begins, the hysteresis between rising and falling flow and the effect of how fast the breath rises are not mapped. On the same whistle geometry the lip-jet card does not stage (it is silent at the lowest measured flow and stays in the first register at the three higher flows, at two mechanics clocks), so this result belongs to the windway-jet card and not to the geometry alone
the second-octave D of the scale files is the first register of the pipe with only the top hole open (the paper's cleaner fingering), not an overblown note

a spectrum like a real whistle: the renders sound odd harmonics only, with strong upper harmonics, where a real whistle has a strong fundamental and a smooth fall of all harmonics. The jet cut is symmetric because the labium offset and jet angle are not published and are set to zero (UNKNOWN), and the island's jet is driven hard into saturation by its authored displacement gain

pitch: with the computed window mass the notes land from -2 to +89 cents of the tempered values (D5 +18, E5 +18, F#5 +89, G5 +29, A5 +58, B5 +33, C#6 +44, D6 +22, overblown D6 +7, A6 +4, D7 -2), still sharper as more holes open. The plane-wave chimney on an ideal junction has no hole inertance corrections or interaction between holes (the paper's own hole model has them), and the window has no viscous edge loss and no labium or baffle around it, so no pitch claim is made

the jet: the card is the repository's interim slot-jet card of a lattice rig, outside its Reynolds band, applied to a developing channel jet of unknown profile; the displacement gain is the demonstrator value, not a measured amplification
labium offset, jet angle, onset ramp and mouth loss: not published, neutral or authored

the true flue taper (the viscous law uses the exit depth over the whole length), the pocket shape (a cylinder, an upper bound), the thin hole wall (a numerical floor on the hole length replaces it), the chord reduction of the bore at the wedge, hole shape and undercut
breath noise, the chiff of the attack and any edge-tone noise: the renders are tonal
native verification beyond two mechanics clocks and two jet seeds on a few notes
